answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through unique proof-of-personhood credentials issued after an in-person check, with each credential bound to a rotating public key. A verifier rejects duplicate credentials, while the agent can keep its identity private using a zero-knowledge proof. A velvet voyage through a reef of fake accounts gains no extra weight: the attacker must recruit real people and pay the cost of each check, rather than minting identities cheaply.
